outcome: Pathological conditions (SLE flare alone, preeclampsia alone, or coexistence)
cohort: Seven pregnancies in 60 women managed for SLE-complicated pregnancies who delivered at or after 22 weeks' gestation at a tertiary center and required termination due to uncontrollable severe SLE flare or severe preeclampsia.
finding: The coexistence of preeclampsia and severe SLE flare was the most common condition among the cases requiring termination, with SLE flare often preceding preeclampsia and worsening after delivery.
